ic_name: HDMI / DVI TMDS (TI TFP410 PanelBus Digital Transmitter — subset)
frame_transmit_sequence: 1. Power-on: DV_DD / PV_DD / TV_DD ramp to 3.3 V; ISEL/RST held LOW during ramp.
2. ISEL/RST released HIGH: I2C interface enabled; all RW registers go to defaults; CTL_1_MODE.PD = 0 → device powered down.
3. Host I2C controller writes CTL_1_MODE = {TDIS=0, VEN=1, HEN=1, DSEL/BSEL/EDGE per config, PD=1} to enable normal operation.
4. PLL begins locking to IDCK; t_lock several µs; during lock TMDS output is invalid.
5. (Optional) Host reads EDID from receiver: I2C controller targets DDC at 0xA0; reads 128 bytes; selects supported video format.
6. Host sets HSYNC polarity (HS_POL), VSYNC polarity (VS_POL) via DE_CTL; optionally enables DE generator (DE_GEN=1, DE_DLY, DE_CNT, DE_TOP, DE_LIN).
7. Graphics controller drives IDCK + DATA + DE + HSYNC + VSYNC.
8. Begin of frame: VSYNC active edge resets internal vertical line counter.

9. Vertical-blanking lines (DE=0): for each pixel, TFP410 emits control characters on TX0/TX1/TX2 (DVI mode). HDMI mode would emit video preamble + guard band + audio data island + null packets but these are OUTSIDE TFP410 scope.

10. Active video lines: HSYNC active edge resets horizontal pixel counter. DE rises HIGH for the active region of the line. For each pixel: encode B[7:0]→TX0, G[7:0]→TX1, R[7:0]→TX2 via 8→10 transition-minimised + DC-balance.
11. End of active region of line: DE returns LOW; resume control-character emission for horizontal blanking.
12. Repeat 10-11 for every active line of the frame.
13. After last active line, vertical-blanking lines continue with control characters until next VSYNC active edge.
14. Loop back to step 8 for next frame.
receiver_state_machine_sequence: 1. Receiver initially in loss-of-lock; HPD output is LOW if unpowered or disconnected.
2. Receiver powers up; HPD pull-up drives HPD HIGH; cable connection signals presence to source.
3. Receiver PLL locks on TXC (recovers pixel clock).
4. Receiver internal 10× multiplier generates bit clock (or PLL recovers bit clock directly).
5. Receiver hunts for control-character codes (high transition density: 7 transitions over 10 bits) during DE=low blanking.
6. Receiver byte-aligns by recognising one of the 4 Channel-0 control codes (0x354/0x0AB/0x154/0x2AB).
7. Receiver enters decode loop: per pixel clock, sample each TX channel's 10-bit symbol.
8. If 10-bit symbol matches a control character code → DE=0 (blanking); decode {VSYNC,HSYNC,CTL[3:1]}.
9. Else → DE=1 (active video); decode 10b → 8b: undo inversion if bit[9]=1; undo XOR/XNOR cascade per bit[8]; recover original 8-bit pixel byte.
10. Reassemble pixel from TX0=B, TX1=G, TX2=R.
11. Output pixel + recovered HSYNC/VSYNC + DE to display panel timing controller.
12. Continue per IDCK period; receiver tracks running disparity per channel (mirror of source's encoder state).
13. On loss of TXC clock or loss of control-character lock → return to step 3 (re-lock).
i2c_register_access_sequence: 1. Host issues Start condition on SCL/SDA.
2. Host drives 7-bit target write address 0b0111_A3A2A1 + R/W=0 → 0x70..0x7E.
3. TFP410 ACKs (pulls SDA LOW on 9th clock).
6. (Write) Host drives data byte; TFP410 latches into register; auto-increments sub-address. Repeat for multi-byte writes.
8. (Read) After step 5, host issues Restart; sends 7-bit read address 0x71..0x7F; TFP410 ACKs; TFP410 drives data byte; host ACKs for next-byte continuation or NAKs to end read.
ddc_edid_read_sequence: 1. Host I2C controller (NOT TFP410 itself — the host uses the same I2C bus through TFP410's open-drain SCL/SDA wires) issues Start.
4. Host writes sub-address 0x00 (start of EDID block).
6. Host issues Restart; writes 7-bit address 0x50 + R=1 → 0xA1.
7. Receiver ACKs; transmits 128 bytes of EDID block; host NAKs the 128th byte to end.
9. Host parses EDID: detailed timing, supported video formats, manufacturer ID, etc.; selects best mode.
hpd_change_sequence: 1. Receiver supplies HPD HIGH (3.3 V) when powered + connected.
2. Source samples HPD via EDGE/HTPLG pin (ISEL=1) and reflects in CTL_2_MODE.HTPLG.
3. On HPD logic-level change, MDI bit fires (if TSEL=1 selecting HTPLG); interrupt asserted on MSEN pin (if MSEL programmed accordingly).
4. Host responds: if HPD high → re-read EDID + resume TMDS output; if HPD low → optionally gate TMDS to V_OFF.
5. Host writes MDI=1 to clear the latched interrupt.
deskew_calibration_sequence: 1. Host enables CTL_3_MODE.DKEN=1 (or asserts DKEN pin HIGH with ISEL=0).
2. Host writes DK[3:1] code (000..111) into CTL_3_MODE bits 7:5.
3. Internal latch-window for DATA[23:0] shifted by t_CD = (DK[3:1] - 4) × t_STEP ≈ (-1.4 ns to +1.05 ns).
4. Iterate DK code while monitoring receiver eye / TMDS output; pick best center.
5. Repeat per environment / supply-voltage / temperature corner if needed.
power_down_and_wake_sequence: 1. Host writes CTL_1_MODE.PD=0 → TFP410 enters power-down; TMDS outputs go to V_OFF; PLL gated.
2. Host writes CTL_1_MODE.PD=1 → PLL begins re-locking (few µs); TMDS valid after lock.
3. For fast gating without full power-down, use CTL_1_MODE.TDIS=1 (PLL stays locked); set TDIS=0 to re-enable TMDS drivers immediately.
